'''Raymond Woodard Brink''' (4 January 1890 in [[Newark, New Jersey]] &ndash; 27 December 1973 in [[La Jolla, California]]) was an American mathematician. His Ph.D. advisor at [[Harvard]] was [[George David Birkhoff]].

Brink entered [[Kansas State University|Kansas State College]] at age 14 and by age 19 had two [[bachelor's degree]]s<ref name=maapres/> and was employed as an instructor of mathematics in [[Moscow, Idaho]]; he taught at the state preparatory school of the [[University of Idaho]].<ref name=gem11>{{cite web|url=http://issuu.com/uidahodigital/docs/gem1911/13|publisher=Gem or the Mountains, University of Idaho yearbook|title=Instructors, etc.|date=May 1910|page=9}}</ref><ref name=crbrwb95>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=6M0qAAAAIBAJ&sjid=6NAFAAAAIBAJ&pg=3817,1310919|newspaper=Moscow-Pullman Daily News|last=Laboe|first=Barbara|title=Brink's son in Moscow for party|date=October 19, 1995|page=1A}}</ref> He returned to school  at [[Harvard University|Harvard]] and earned a doctorate in 1916 and was a longtime professor at the [[University of Minnesota]], and also authored numerous math textbooks. He served as president of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] from 1941&ndash;42.<ref name=maapres>{{cite web|url=http://www.maa.org/history/presidents/brink.html|publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|title=Raymond Woodard Brink, 1941-1942 MAA President|accessdate=November 18, 2012}}</ref>

==Personal==
Brink was the husband of author [[Carol Ryrie Brink]], whom he had met during his first year in Idaho when both were teenagers.  She was nearly six years his junior; they wed nine years later in 1918, following her graduation from college.<ref name=crbrwb95/> Married for over 55 years at the time of his death, they had two children, [[David R. Brink|David]] and Nora (Hunter).<ref name=crbpkded95>{{cite news|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=N7VeAAAAIBAJ&sjid=ITAMAAAAIBAJ&pg=5109,1348719|newspaper=Lewiston (ID) Morning Tribune|last=Johnson|first=David|title=Nature park dedicated at Moscow|date=October 21, 1995|page=7A}}</ref> David (b. 1919) became an attorney and later headed the [[American Bar Association]].<ref name=curb>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1981/11/12/us/bar-leader-fears-crisis-over-curbs-on-courts.html|newspaper=The New York Times|last=Taylor|first=Stuart Jr.|title=Bar leader fears crisis over curbs on courts|date=November 12, 1981|page=A24}}</ref><ref name=startrib>{{cite web|url=http://www.startribune.com/local/west/132897408.html|work=StarTribune.com|title=At 92, he's a man of the word|last=Smetanka|first=Mary Jane|date=November 3, 2011|accessdate=November 18, 2012}}</ref>
